description:
In class on 2023/11/13, we demonstrated the QuTools Entanglement Demonstrator. You should have captured the output screen on the device showing the counts for the 16 different detector settings.

Note that Prof. Van Meter explained the CHSH calculation incorrectly in class that day; the correct entries and their meaning are shown here:

 

Answer the following questions:

  1. Explain why there are sixteen settings (instead of some other number like four or nine or 35 or 36). You will need to explain what it means to measure a +1 or -1 eigenvalue when using polarization photonic qubits.
  2. List the sixteen settings as polarization measurement angles. Identify which angles correspond to which entries in Table 10.1 in the excerpt from the book above.
  3. Express those settings as measurement bases on the Bloch (or Poincaré) sphere.
  4. Calculate the S value for the CHSH inequality as above using the data from the QuTools demonstration.
  5. (Bonus: Toward the end of the Quantum Internet QOLS module, you will see a brief discussion of loopholes in the discussion of Bell inequality violations such as CHSH. Learn about those and describe which loopholes are and are not closed by the QuTools demonstration.)
name: CHSH Inequality Calculation
